Combine grounding tokens worst-case

Source: R/grounding.R
combine_grounding.Rd

Reduces the tokens of several input facts to the token of a verdict that rests on all of them. The combination is worst-case: the verdict is grounded only when every input is grounded.

Usage

combine_grounding(tokens)

Arguments

tokens

A character vector of grounding tokens, each of which should be GROUNDING_GROUNDED or GROUNDING_UNVERIFIED. The token emitted up to 0.1.0 and any unrecognised string are treated as not grounded, which is the safe reading. A zero-length vector is valid and means "the verdict rests on nothing checked".

Value

A length-1 character vector: GROUNDING_GROUNDED when every token is grounded, GROUNDING_UNVERIFIED otherwise.

Details

Worst-case combination is what stops a grounding label from being laundered through a pipeline. Any other rule – a majority, a mean, an optimistic "at least one" – would let a verdict inherit confidence from the checked inputs while quietly resting on an unchecked one. As with grounding_token, an empty set of inputs is unverified rather than vacuously grounded.

See also

grounding_token for minting a token from verification dates.

Author

Max Moldovan

Examples

combine_grounding(c(GROUNDING_GROUNDED, GROUNDING_GROUNDED))
#> [1] "grounded"
combine_grounding(c(GROUNDING_GROUNDED, GROUNDING_UNVERIFIED))
#> [1] "ungrounded"
combine_grounding(character(0))
#> [1] "ungrounded"
